elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph covers only professional liability (E&O) and cyber/privacy liability; no commercial general liability limit appears anywhere in the rendered text or elsewhere in Article XVIII.

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: No aggregate CGL limit is stated; the insertion names only two coverages (E&O USD 1,000,000; cyber USD 2,000,000).

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted language sets E&O at 'not less than USD 1,000,000', below the preferred USD 2,000,000 threshold.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: Cyber and privacy liability is set at 'not less than USD 2,000,000', below the preferred USD 5,000,000.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: No workers' compensation obligation appears in the inserted paragraph or the retained 18.14 text; the comment expressly acknowledges it was omitted.

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: No certificate-on-request mechanic is included; the comment states it was intentionally left out.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: 'Array shall maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000' — Array is the counterparty/licensor, so the obligation runs in the correct party direction and meets the floor.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: '...and cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000' — express cyber/privacy coverage at the fallback amount, imposed on Array.

reasons: The finding of 'missing' is corroborated: the cited Article XVIII text ends at 18.14 with no coverage covenant, and the only other insurance references are Net Sales deduction mentions in Article I, which impose no obligation.
Fallback is complete: both atomic elements (E&O ≥ USD 1,000,000; cyber and privacy ≥ USD 2,000,000) are expressed as unconditional maintenance obligations on Array, the counterparty.

Preferred is not complete: CGL per-occurrence and aggregate limits, the USD 2,000,000 E&O limit, the USD 5,000,000 cyber limit, workers' compensation and certificates on request are all absent from operative language and are only gestured at in the margin comment, which cannot satisfy an element.

Minimality holds: the insertion is a single sentence limited to the two fallback coverages, and it correctly omits model-language extras (at-own-expense, the one-year survival tail, certificates) that no selected element requires. No existing wording, including all of 18.14, was deleted or paraphrased.
Intent is preserved: the new paragraph sits after 18.14, introduces no defined term, cross-reference or timing mechanic, and does not contradict the indemnity/recall allocation in Article XVI.

Drafting nit for repair (not a minimality or completeness failure): the rendered insertion carries only the heading 'Insurance.' with no section number, while the comment refers to 'Section 18.15' — number the new paragraph 18.15 so the reference in the comment matches the operative text. Consider also adding a duration anchor ('throughout the Term') so the obligation is not open to an argument that it can lapse immediately after signature.
